B.S. Mechanical Engineering · Minor in Data Science

Based in Los Angeles and currently studying Mechanical Engineering at UC Berkeley with a minor in Data Science. I am drawn to the intersection of robotics, engineering, and the real world around us. I love taking genuine knowledge of real problems and engineering practical, accessible solutions to them. As a certified scuba diver and marine conservationist, much of my work is focused on designing a better ocean, though I am actively exploring all fields and committed to learning as much as I can throughout my undergraduate years. I am someone who loves connecting with people, and I am always looking to learn from and contribute to every community I am a part of. Feel free to reach out!

Projects

Built From Scratch

Every project starts with a real problem. Most of mine start in or near the ocean.

UC Berkeley · Jan–May 2026 · Individual Project

Wave Energy Collector

Solo Designer and Engineer

Designed a small-scale wave energy harvesting device from scratch, converting ocean wave heave into electricity using a rack-and-pinion mechanism coupled to a permanent magnet alternator, with modularity and field deployability as core design requirements.

Purpose-built to power remote ocean sensing and monitoring equipment at sea. Every design decision was shaped by real ocean conditions: daily direction reversals, wave-induced uplift and lateral loading, subsystem alignment under realistic loading, and the need for fully waterproofed, modular systems that can be serviced in the field.

  • Designed a two-DOF drive system with rubber-bushed rod guides and chamfered gear teeth to handle the daily mechanical stresses of direction reversals caused by wave oscillation
  • Engineered a catenary mooring with a spiked anchor plate to resist wave-induced uplift and lateral loading forces
  • Decoupled mechanical and electrical subsystems for modularity and constrained float motion to maintain rack-pinion pitch line alignment under realistic ocean wave loading
  • Fully waterproofed all systems and designed for straightforward field servicing
SolidWorksOcean EngineeringEnergy HarvestingWaterproofingMooring Design

UC Berkeley · Feb–Apr 2026 · Team Project

Smart Waste Sorting System

Project Lead, Mechanical Focus

Led a cross-disciplinary team across Mechanical Engineering, EECS, and Data Science to design and build a fully automated waste sorter integrating LLM-based image classification, from blank page to working system.

Managed the full engineering process including ideation, scheduling, GANTT charts, BOMs, cross-team integration, CAD, and fabrication. The mechanical system captures and positions objects, triggers a real-time LLM image classification query, and routes the item to the correct compartment via Arduino-controlled dual servo motors.

  • Engineered the intake and imaging mechanism that reliably captures and positions objects for accurate LLM classification
  • Led all CAD design in SolidWorks and drove multiple fitment refinement iterations through to final assembly
  • Generated and maintained all BOMs, mechanical documentation, and project schedule; coordinated across subteams throughout the build cycle
SolidWorksArduinoLLM IntegrationProject LeadSystems Integration

Palos Verdes, CA · 2021–2025 · Independent Research

Optimizing Coral Substrate Design for Ocean Resilience

Independent Researcher · NOAA Recognized

Designed, fabricated, and tested 12 variants of 3D-printed artificial reef substrates, achieving a 43% increase in coral larvae attachment rates compared to natural substrates.

Exploring how engineered surfaces can accelerate coral reef recovery, I developed and iterated on substrate designs with varied surface textures and biopolymer materials. Each variant was physically tested for larvae attachment in controlled conditions, with results guiding the next design iteration.

  • Designed 12 unique substrate variants using 3D printing, systematically varying surface texture patterns and biopolymer material compositions
  • Tested each variant for coral larvae attachment rates, achieving a 43% improvement over natural baseline substrates
3D PrintingBiopolymersReef EngineeringOcean ConservationIterative Testing

Palos Verdes, CA · 2021–2025 · Independent Research

Coral Reef Bleaching Prediction System

Independent Researcher · NASA Recognized

Corrected systematic errors in NASA satellite sea surface temperature data by reconciling them against in-situ field measurements, then used the corrected dataset to build a machine learning model that predicts future coral bleaching-prone regions with significantly improved accuracy and speed.

Satellite data for coral reef monitoring contained systematic discrepancies that made bleaching predictions unreliable. By diving 14 sites across the Pacific and collecting in-situ turbidity and temperature measurements, I identified and corrected those errors, producing a cleaner dataset, then trained a predictive model on that corrected data to identify which reef regions are most at risk of bleaching in the future.

  • Collected in-situ data across 14 reef sites and reconciled measurements against NASA Landsat-8 satellite data to identify and correct systematic discrepancies, improving bleaching prediction accuracy by 31% and reducing false-positive alerts
  • Trained a Random Forest model on the corrected dataset spanning 8 years and 3 ocean regions to predict future bleaching-prone sites, achieving 4x faster risk assessment and 27% improvement in predictive precision
Machine LearningPythonNASA Landsat-8Field ResearchRandom ForestOcean Conservation
